the interaction of CFTR and Ca2+-activated channels in endothelial cells.
the interaction between the CaCC and CF TR.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CFTR-Ca2+-activated Cl− channel interaction requires the presence of the R-domain and that it is mediated by the C-terminus of the R-domain.
the C-terminal R domain of CFTR is important to the activity of CFTR, but not the interaction of CFTR with CaCC.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interaction of CFTR and Ca2+-activated chloride channels (CaCCs) is mediated by the R-domain of CFTR and that the PDZ binding domain of CFTR is not involved.
CFTR-Ca2+ channel interaction requires the C-terminal part, but not the C-terminal PDZ binding motif of CFTR.
CFTR inhibits the CaCC activity by a mechanism that involves the C-terminal part but not the PD2 binding motif of the R-domain.

CFTR inhibits CaCC by a mechanism that is independent of CFTR phosphorylation.
the C-terminal end of the R-domain of CFTR is important for CFTR-CACC interaction.
